entry.summary: Visa-free short stays as part of the Schengen area. Germany and Australia also have a bilateral visa exemption agreement: read the German Embassy's page on how it adds to Schengen time.
entry.max_stay: 90 days in any 180-day period across the Schengen area
entry.pre_arrival: None today. ETIAS is on the watch list.
entry.other: Schengen Entry/Exit System: fingerprints and photo at the border on first entry (free, nothing to do beforehand). Get an entry stamp where one is still given, and carry your passport across internal borders.

tourism.detail: Australians may stay for up to 90 days in any 180-day period, subject to entry conditions and the shared Schengen count.
tourism.next: Check passport validity, return plans and the rolling Schengen total immediately before travel.
tourism.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

meetings.route: Visa-free business visit; section 16/30 protection where its foreign-employer test fits
meetings.detail: Section 16 covers qualifying meetings, negotiations, offers, contracts and contract monitoring for a foreign employer while habitual residence remains abroad, up to 90 days in 180; section 30 says that bounded activity is not employment for residence-law purposes.
meetings.next: Carry an overseas-employer or enterprise letter and keep the first visit to discussion, negotiation, contracting and observation rather than delivery.
meetings.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

conference.detail: Attendance and networking can use the short-stay front door; the ordinary visa waiver does not turn an attendee into a worker, trainer or programmed speaker.
conference.next: Carry registration and the organiser invitation, and reclassify the trip if a talk, workshop or paid duty is added.
conference.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

unpaid-speaking.route: Sections 22 and 30 for a qualifying short lecture or special academic or artistic appearance
unpaid-speaking.detail: A person retaining habitual residence abroad may give lectures or performances of special academic or artistic value for no more than 90 days in 12 months without the activity being treated as employment under the Residence Act. Lack of a fee is not the legal test.
unpaid-speaking.next: Have the host record why the appearance has special academic or artistic value and confirm the exception where the fit is debatable.
unpaid-speaking.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

paid-speaking.route: The same narrow section 22/30 exception where every condition genuinely fits; otherwise obtain work-authorised residence status
paid-speaking.detail: The statutory exception is framed by activity, value, residence abroad and duration rather than by a zero-fee rule. Ordinary paid consulting, facilitation or commercial delivery does not automatically become a qualifying lecture.
paid-speaking.next: Put the fee, expenses, format and duties in the invitation and obtain written confirmation before relying on the exception.
paid-speaking.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

book-launch.route: Business visit for rights and publisher meetings; section 22 where a qualifying lecture or literary performance fits
book-launch.detail: Rights negotiation and partner meetings can stay in the business lane. A reading, talk, workshop, direct retail operation and imported stock should be classified separately.
book-launch.next: Use a German publisher or bookseller for local stock and receipts, and have the host classify each public appearance.
book-launch.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

ai-teaching.route: Section 22 for a genuine short lecture of special academic value; work-authorised residence for recurring teaching or training
ai-teaching.detail: A guest lecture can fit the short exception, while a course, continuing corporate training or role embedded in a German institution is a different activity.
ai-teaching.next: Ask the university, conference or company to describe the audience, curriculum, duration and institutional relationship before choosing the route.
ai-teaching.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

remote-work.route: No dedicated digital-nomad route identified; use a freelance, self-employed or employment residence permit where eligible
remote-work.detail: The general visa waiver expressly excludes taking up gainful employment and should not be treated as permission to establish an overseas remote-work base in Germany.
remote-work.next: If Germany becomes a base, choose and obtain the appropriate residence permit before beginning routine work there.
remote-work.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

entrepreneur.route: Residence permit for self-employed business or freelance activity
entrepreneur.detail: A commercial founder must show economic interest or regional need, positive economic effects and finance; freelancers show funding, lawful professional activity and other route-specific evidence. Australians may apply after visa-free entry, but must wait for authorisation before operating.
entrepreneur.next: Choose commercial business or liberal-profession freelance status, prepare the business and finance evidence, and book the local foreigners-authority process before travel.
entrepreneur.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

trade.route: Section 16 meetings and negotiations first; residence, company, tax and customs layers for local delivery
trade.detail: Offers, contracts, negotiation and contract monitoring can fit the short business lane. Installation, hands-on service, local selling and running a German operation are separate.
trade.next: Use the first trip for partners and contracts, then map who imports, invoices, delivers and carries local operating responsibility.
trade.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

artist.route: Section 22/30 for qualifying short special performances, festivals or guest appearances; artist employment or freelance residence for broader work
artist.detail: Special artistic performances and festival or cultural-event work can use the bounded 90-day exception; one-day events have a separate 15-day annual rule. Longer or ordinary entertainment employment needs the relevant route.
artist.next: Have the promoter classify the production, number of days, artistic value, payment and whether the role is employed or self-employed.
artist.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

mixed-mission.route: Visa-free front door with a separate legal basis for each active item
mixed-mission.detail: Tourism, attendance, negotiations and a qualifying lecture can share one visit only when each stays inside its own published boundary. Consulting, remote work, teaching, retail and performance should not be blurred together.
mixed-mission.next: Build one dated schedule and mark every item tourism, attendance, section 16 business, section 22 lecture or performance, or permit-required work.
mixed-mission.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

filming.route: Visa-free Schengen short stay (journalistic or media purposes)
filming.detail: Journalistic or media purposes are listed among visa-free purposes; paid production work and location permits are national matters.
filming.next: Ask the Embassy of the Federal Republic of Germany, Yarralumla about filming, and the local authority about locations.

research.route: Visa-free Schengen short stay (short-term study or training)
research.detail: Short-term study and training are covered; paid research at an institution is paid activity.
research.next: Ask the Embassy of the Federal Republic of Germany, Yarralumla if the host pays you.

volunteering.route: Visa-free visit, within 90 days in 12 months
volunteering.detail: Visa-exempt visitors may do qualifying voluntary or charitable work for up to 90 days in a 12-month period within the Schengen limit. Longer volunteering needs a national visa.

money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: The currency in Germany is the Euro (EUR). If you're travelling between Germany and non-EU countries, declare amounts over 10,000 euros or equivalent. You don't need to declare it if you travel to or from another EU country.

visa-preparation.fastest_entry: Visa-free short stays (90 days or less) as part of the Schengen area, in some cases.
visa-preparation.before_departure: Nothing to lodge before travel today: EES registration happens at the border. ETIAS hadn't started on 2026-11-01.
steps: Germany is in the Schengen area: short stays of 90 days or less can be visa-free in some cases; other purposes or longer stays need a visa before travel.
At the first Schengen border, give fingerprints and a photo for the Entry/Exit System (EES). It's free; nothing is needed before arrival, and sites charging for it are fraudulent.
Carry your passport when crossing borders, including inside Schengen (temporary internal checks are in place in places).
A German-Australian visa exemption agreement exists; check its terms with the German Embassy Canberra. Non-travelling parents can sign a consent form for children.

baseline_unverified.host_unlock: A German organiser can document the academic or artistic value, overseas professional role, habitual residence abroad and exact duration, then confirm the section 22/30 treatment with the competent mission or foreigners authority where the facts are not plain.
baseline_unverified.before_departure: Count all Schengen days and obtain an invitation stating every duty, venue, fee, expense and date. Test any lecture or performance against sections 22 and 30 of the Employment Ordinance before accepting it.
baseline_unverified.useful_stay: The ordinary short-stay ceiling is 90 days in 180. A qualifying lecture or special academic or artistic performance must also stay within 90 days in a 12-month period.
baseline_unverified.from: Luke's earlier precursor notes; not verified against an official source and not an authority. Kept because no official page covers this point yet.

culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: Be punctual: even a few minutes late can offend. Separate rubbish for recycling. Don't press alcohol on someone who has declined it (legal drinking age is 16 for beer and wine, 18 for spirits). Saunas and some pools or park areas are textile-free (nude) at set times, with no sexual meaning.
culture-and-protocol.greetings_and_words: Greet everyone in small shops and waiting rooms with 'Guten Tag', and leave with 'Auf Wiedersehen'. Shake hands on arrival and departure. Use 'Sie' and family names until invited to use 'du'. Don't use 'Fräulein'. When sharing a table, ask 'Ist dieser Platz noch frei?' and wish others 'Guten Appetit'.

drone-pilot-pathway.summary: EU baseline (EASA): register once as an operator in the state of residence or establishment, recognised across EASA states; Specific-category work in another state needs cross-border acceptance by that state's authority. National register, zone map and visitor rules checked 6 Nov 2026 (see items); footage routes not yet checked.

items.text: Not yet checked: whether the national aviation authority publishes a list of authorised operators.

EU rules (Regulations 2019/947 and 2019/945): operators register in the EASA state where they reside or are established; Specific-category operations need an operational authorisation or a standard-scenario declaration.

An operator registered in another EASA state may fly here; for Specific-category work it first gets the authorisation or STS declaration at home, then the destination authority must confirm the cross-border operation before flying. Rules for operators from outside EASA states: not yet checked.
Not yet checked: national tourism board or film commission media libraries.

Operators with their main residence in Germany register with the Luftfahrt-Bundesamt (LBA, the federal aviation office) through its online portal, linked from dipul.de. Registration is needed for drones of 250 g or more, or any drone with a camera or other sensor that records personal data. The LBA says German operator registrations are valid in other EU states. Where a visiting non-resident registers: not stated on the pages read.
The official map of flight zones is dipul, the Digital Platform for Unmanned Aviation (maptool-dipul.dfs.de). The LBA recommends checking it before each flight.

The German National Tourist Board (GNTB) image and video database is free for promoting travel to Germany, after online registration and acceptance of its terms. A search summary of the terms says third parties may use it for their own media, press and editorial pieces on Germany, videos must carry GNTB branding, and billboards, merchandise and books need separate permission. Aerial footage is not mentioned; the terms PDF could not be read directly.
